summary: Adams County, PA steel tower built 1914 and removed 1933 per the FFLOS register; no coordinates, staffing or present-day description found.

facts.status_note: The register says the tower was removed in 1933. No source describes what remains today.

events.note: Register says the steel tower was built in 1914
Register says the tower was removed in 1933
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

evidence.supports: steel tower built 1914 and removed 1933; the register says nothing about remains or access
evidence.quote: This steel tower was built in 1914 and removed in 1933.

notes_for_editor: One source: the FFLOS register entry, which gives the 1914 build, the 1933 removal and the 2008 registration. No staffing, fire or present-day source was found, so the story is short and leaves those out. Not used: (1) a search snippet quoting a 2005 Forest Fire Lookout Association report (firelookout.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/cr-pa-2005.pdf) that calls a 1914 'Piney Mountain Fire Tower' the first state-built steel fire tower in Pennsylvania; the PDF returned no text when fetched, so it cannot be quoted or checked here. (2) The Forest Lookouts page for a 1914 steel 'Pine Mountain' tower in Franklin County (easternuslookouts.weebly.com/pine-mountain3.html), dismantled in 1932 and moved to Little Mountain: a different name and county, not merged. An editor may want to confirm whether the 1914 steel tower is the same structure as this one. (3) A Cumberland County Historical Society photo titled 'Adams - Mountain Fire on Piney Mtn., Near Wenksville': it shows a mountain fire, not the tower, and no date appeared in the text we read. The brief's coordinates are an approximate GNIS name match, not from the register. Confidence low.
